title: Day of Rebirth
subtitle: Fire leaps upon my skin. A blurry past, now clear as day. That is my true identity.

trails.title: Uluru Desert
trails.description: Her guidance came from that which she had awakened long ago, and her protection came from that which she had once saved.

trails.title: The Torch Guardians IV
trails.description: The torch relay comes to a halt here. The flickering flames have enraged the filth beneath the riverbed.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Mmm. Hey! I see it! Over there!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: It's beautiful, even more beautiful than the one I saw in my dream.
Uluru Desert
A Grayhound bus closes its doors and drives away, honking and leaving the girls standing by the road in a puff of dust and smoke.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: This is a miracle of nature like the Great Barrier Reef. Of course, it's pleasing to the eye.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Many would wrestle with the heatwave and travel all the way here from Alice Spring by bus.
Desert Flannel puts down her sunglasses on her head and flips her hair over her face.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Hah. I have to admit, it is worth the effort.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The temperature here will get even higher at noon.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ezra has prepared plenty of Cooling Tablets and water in the medical kit for us. If anyone still suffers sunstroke, we also have the Budgerigar Coat as an emergency measure.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: So that's why Ezra took you to the room before we left? To tell you all these?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ezra is worried about you, and so are we.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Hmph.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Ooh. Someone is feeling bad about what she said earlier.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: If you ask me, that human girl has a good heart. Maybe she can work on her ways of communicating with people, but that altruism in her is almost angel-like.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: And she has the face of a little angel. Wouldn't be such a bad idea to put her in some baby care commercials. I heard those things pay you generously. I might as well ask what she thinks.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Flame
items.text: Go forward.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Wow! It's talking again!

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: What? Who's talking again?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: The flame! It's talking! Didn't you hear it?!

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Nah, it sounds the same to me. This is just the sound of fire burning, snoring, like my late old man.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Well, maybe you can also try turning off this little thingy's TV. Maybe it will jump up and shout "I'm still watching."

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I'm not joking! It's really talking! Listen!
Lifting the flame with both of her hands, Spathodea puts it as close to Desert Flannel's ear as possible.
Desert Flannel looks more and more alarmed in the silence.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Wait. Its temperature has gone up, and ... it's transforming? What is this, a rocket?

items.speaker: Flame
items.text: No more waiting.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Whoa!
As swift as an arrow, the burning fireball radiating heat waves flies towards the other side of the desert.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Hey, hang on! Where are you going?!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I thought we were good friends! Are you ditching me already?!
The agile Spathodea is the first to catch up with the flame.
Behind them, the Grayhound bus in the distance is starting again.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Everyone, mind your steps and keep up!

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: A race in the desert. Great. I wonder why I'm not as clever and creative as you are.
The noisy crowd has gone. Where they once were, a slim figure pops out of a tree.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Ms. Vertin ... Was she talking to me? She always looks over, perhaps she knows that I'm following them.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: But ... no. I'm hiding well. They shouldn't know.
Mumbling, Ezra sketches a fire pattern into his notebook.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Having emotional turmoil, acting impulsively, feeling fanatical about the retrieved memories ... and the unstoppable urge to return to the "homeland."

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: These all match the description in the research notes.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: And now, the fire, which is also the key in this case, is burning vigorously.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: The notes end here. That's all we know about "reincarnators."
Looking up into the distance, Ezra walks from one bush to another.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: I can't deduce more based on the current data, but at the same time, the unknown can be dangerous yet exciting. It might bring about catastrophes or miracles.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Just like arcanists, so charming and lively.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: My job is to help and protect them, so their burning enthusiasm will not be dampened. Like what Mom said, this is our mission as mankind.
The human child once again opens the backpack and checks it for the 1,001st time.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: The Annular Jumper Frog Mushroom, the Fairy Ring Powders, and the Butterfly-shaped Portobello Mushroom ... Very well, I have them all. This time, I'm prepared for any danger.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Hah! Gotcha! You are not running away from ...

items.speaker: Flame
items.text: This is ... the beginning ... of the journey.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Beginning of the journey? No, we set off from Melbourne!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: We're close to Uluru now, so it's almost our destin- ...

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Gosh, what are these?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: These are murals. No, they are reliefs. All the marks are carved out of the wall.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: These carvings existed long before any murals, and they are rougher.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Of course, they are. Just think, when did our ancestors learn to draw with paints? And when did they start carving with sharp stones?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: They are beautiful, like star trails, one circle in another.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I think I've seen them before. They feel familiar and make me thirsty at the same time. Look, this circle is just like a spring.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: We don't need a spring. We brought water ourselves. Drink as much as you want.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Hmm. Look here. These are most probably some ancient relics. This one looks like an animal, and this, a plant!

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Emm? And what is this, a birdy?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: They have something to do with people's lives. These marks have to mean something.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Maybe they will lead us to the entrance to the Stadium.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: This is the time when Spathodea's opinion matters more than ours. Come, key girl, take a look at this.
But they can't find the girl who was talking about her thirst anywhere. The water leaking from the fallen dusty-covered cup is absorbed into the hot sand.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Spathodea? Where, where did she go?

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: And that fire, they are all gone!

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: What the hell is going on again? She'd better be pulling a prank on me. I heard her footsteps behind me just now.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Relax, Desert Flannel. We've got help.
A slim figure emerges from behind the tree.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Ezra? How, how did you get here? Wait, how long have you been following us?

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: From the beginning, when you were at the hospital. Sorry, Ms. Desert Flannel, please let me check this first.
Ezra frowns, quickening his pace when nearing the wall of reliefs.
Some mushrooms break into pieces under the pressure and release a pungent scent of spores.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: This smell ... I can't be wrong—This is Devil's Thorn.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: What's that? Does it have anything to do with her missing?

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: A rare kind of mushroom that grows in the desert. Allegedly, it's genetically connected to lizards. I've only seen its pictures in books.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: It has wide, open pileus with sharp spikes, and its roots are as absorbent as sponge, which allows it to absorb and preserve underground water. They only appear around water sources, and with this spiral pattern on the wall, I think ...

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: I think I might have a way to find her.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Ezra stands up and takes out a metal dowsing rod from his pocket.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Please come with me.
Thirst. She felt the dry thirst throughout her body. As if she had never taken even a single sip of water, or she was a beast that must keep running and running for its survival.
A gout of flame pierces through the formless dark.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Little flame?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: *coughs* My throat ... It hurts ... Water ...

items.speaker: Flame
items.text: Do you remember me?
The fire pulses and comes closer to her, like a beating heart.

items.speaker: Flame
items.text: I traveled through the endless flood, drought, rain, and waterfalls to finally reach you.

items.speaker: Flame
items.text: Do you remember me?
Her dry throat keeps twitching as if a toad was resting there.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I do, but ... not really ...

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I can't recall your name or your face, but I do remember ...
She curls up in a tight ball. Her palms and feet getting hotter and hotter.

items.speaker: Flame
items.text: Do you remember our fight?
The boiling raindrops mixed with fire are splashed on her spine.
Together, they pour into her dry throat.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Ugh!
She is not sure if she is standing or crawling on the ground. The only thing she can do is breathe like a fish.
The fire flows from the back of her ears to her eyes, like a warm hug from behind.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: "Weigh the anchor of the current feelings and seek in the boundless net."
She hears a different voice coming from her own throat.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: "Seek me, seek the past, seek the intelligence and spirit we are bound to find."

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I don't wanna make up with you! You dumb ball of fire!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: "Neither do I, you stupid girl!"

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: My hands are burning, like they are soaked in fire.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: "That's because you reached into me. We had a fight, attacking each other with nails like two cats."

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Ah! This is just like the day we first met!
The scene in her mind becomes clear. She can see the clue of this ancient memory within her reach.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I can feel my knees trembling again.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I know this game, a sport which is not popular enough to be included in any commercial or professional games.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: It's also the sport for which I've been secretly training myself every day after lunch—the light-bulbs-picking game, Malingee's Harvest ... No, no.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: But these are not light bulbs for the athletes to pick up from the ground, but fire ... And I don't have such a burning campfire at home. It can only be found here.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Beside the flowing spring, under the starry sky, on the scorching sand, I saw the burning campfire and the sparks scattering in all directions.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: My hands surrounded by blazing flames, I touched the inner cone again and again as I flew by. Immersed in great joy, I dove down from the air.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: "At that time, our hands held each other in the flames."

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: "Our traces went on from one torch to another."

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Yes, I know. I remember it now.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I once drank the cold water in the spring and covered my limbs with colorful strips. I sang and danced until a pair of wrinkled hands touched my forehead.
An elderly man staggers to his feet and rises from the depths of the dark cave.

items.speaker: Priest
items.text: Good girl, my good girl ...

items.speaker: Priest
items.text: Your hands are dusted, but you win the game, and your soul is sparkling. It's you who find the hottest fire for us! It's you who connect to it and make friends with it!

items.speaker: Priest
items.text: I shall grant you the scepter and lead you to the highest platform.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I shall become the next Priestess of the Uluru Temple.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I shall take responsibility for every drop of sweat on the red soil, and I shall eulogize all the significant, fair competitions.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I shall store the flame in my mouth, my stomach, my heart, and my ribs.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I shall protect her, not to let her extinguish, nor to let her go astray or away.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I hereby swear ...

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I shall be with the Uluru Games, until ... forever.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: M-Mom ...

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: M-M-Mom never told me ... w-w-we are descendants of the Red Dragon ...
Uluru spring

items.speaker: Critter
items.text: *roars*

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Ah?! I-I'm awake now. This is the entrance to the Stadium!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Then that howl must be ...
The girl bends and rolls on the ground in a circle to avoid the sharp claws' attack.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: The guardians of the Stadium, I knew it! *coughs*

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I'm too weary to stand up! Shoot, there's no way I can beat them just rolling around!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Ms. Spathodea!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: E-Ezra?! And Desert Flannel, Vertin!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Thank goodness you found me!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: These critters—they don't look like any kind that I know of. What are they ...

items.speaker: Critter
items.text: *hiss*
Facing the boulders thrown by the critters, Spathodea does a forward roll and hides behind a shelter.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: These critters are the guardians of the Stadium! They are ... Ugh, I can explain it later. We have to deal with them first!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Hmm? Little flame?! Hey! What are you doing?!
The little flame floats leisurely toward the monsters.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No time to hesitate. Protect Spathodea and engage!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Great, they are down!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Everyone, for the sake of prudence, please stay back and do not approach before confirming the danger has been eliminated.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: No, there's no more danger now. Look!
A heated current of air surges from the top of Uluru Rock to the spring by the people's feet.
Among the remains of a guardian critter, a bone torch is engulfed in the flame.

items.speaker: Flame
items.text: No need to worry or hesitate.
The scorching heat storms around.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Now, it's all clear!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Long story short, mates, I've retrieved many memories. At least now I know who I used to be.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: My name in the last life was Flammy, exactly what my close ones call me now.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I am still ME. I'm not replaced by anyone.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: You are still you, the modern version ...

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: This has never happened to any "reincarnators" as far as we know!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: That's because Flammy and I are very alike, and we both have the same duty on our shoulders.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I am Flammy. I obtained the Uluru Flame from the fire with my own hands. I was the first Priestess in the history of the Uluru Games.

items.speaker: Flame
items.text: I am Spathodea. I keep the flame that traveled all the way from the ancient times inside me. I will become the next Priestess in the history of the Uluru Games.
The flame is no longer the small flame as it was. Now, it is roaring like a beast, rearing up into the sky.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Remember what I said, mates? My flame is our compass!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Mom said good kids never lie. So, I always keep my word!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Spathodea looks back and gives them a grin.
In an instant, she hurries her pace and jumps into the fire.
